comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Premise confirmed empirically from live Reconcile Bridge logs (GitHub Actions).

Four consecutive live passes (runs 31568815075, 31569179421, 31569723185, 31570037358, spanning ~30 min on 2026-08-12) each emit exactly 19 failed inbound link writes: 5 'source ticket is closed', 13 'redundant link — ancestor-descendant relationship', 1 'would create a cycle at epic level'. Normalising the log lines and diffing two of those passes yields a BYTE-IDENTICAL failing set — same source, same target, same relation, same reason. So the reconciler has no memory of the outcome: it re-derives and re-attempts the identical impossible set every pass.

The failing call site is named in every line: rebar_reconciler.apply_inbound_records::_apply_inbound_update — it invokes 'rebar link', catches RebarError, logs WARNING, and continues. That warn-and-continue is the whole of the current handling.

Quantified waste: 19 doomed link writes per pass, passes run continuously (~every 5-6 min), i.e. roughly 200+ known-doomed writes per hour, indefinitely, plus 19 permanent WARNING lines forming the error floor described in the ticket.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Fix pushed as Gerrit change 1641 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1641).

Shape of the change:
- NEW src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/impossible_links.py — classify() maps a link failure to closed_source / redundant_ancestry / cycle, or to None. None is the safety valve: an unrecognised failure is never recorded and keeps today's retry-next-pass behaviour, so a transient fault cannot be misfiled as permanent. ImpossibleLinkStore persists verdicts to .bridge_state/impossible_links.json (a SEPARATE file from bindings.json, so it cannot collide with the peer-confirmation record epic despotic-floriated-leopard plans there).
- The invalidation key is a "deciding digest": a hash over exactly the inputs the three validators read — each endpoint's status, parent chain, and dep set. Reopen the closed source or reparent an endpoint and the digest stops matching, so the link is re-attempted once, unassisted. A comment on an endpoint does NOT invalidate it (tested), or the churn would return by the back door on an active store.
- apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links: ADD branch only — consult the record before spending the write, classify+record after a failure. The REMOVE branch and _inbound_unlink_one are untouched.
- Logging: a newly-recorded impossible link still WARNs once (a genuinely new one stays loud); repeat skips become one INFO summary per pass naming the store path. The permanent WARNING floor drains without anything being hidden.

Overlap check vs despotic-floriated-leopard: NO conflict. That epic owns the inbound REMOVAL path (_inbound_unlink_one, differ G3/G4/G5) and a peer-confirmation record in the binding store; this owns the inbound ADD path and a distinct state file. The two are complementary and neither reads the other's record.

Verification: the headline test counts rebar.link invocations across two passes against a REAL store (pass 1 = 1 attempt, pass 2 = 0), deliberately not asserting on log text, since a log-shaped assertion would also pass for mere suppression. RED was confirmed by temporarily disabling the skip: 3 behavioural cells fail without it. 14 new tests pass; 2397 reconciler tests green; make lint and make typecheck exit 0.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Review round 1: LLM-Review -1 on change 1641, now addressed. Live change is 1646 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1646); 1641 abandoned as superseded (amending lost the Change-Id, so the follow-up opened a new change rather than PS2).

The -1 was bugfix-size-attestation: 385 non-test lines, over the 150-line bug-fix floor, with no plan-review attestation on this ticket. Earning it surfaced three real defects — the gate paid for itself rather than being a formality:

1. BLOCKING (would have shipped a broken fix): the record file was never committed to the tickets branch. reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot stages only bindings.json, bindings-retired.json and get_rotation.json. Every reconcile pass runs in a FRESH CI checkout, so a record living only in the working tree is discarded between passes — the skip would never take effect in production and the bug would have outlived the fix with every unit test still green. Fixed: added git_adapter.IMPOSSIBLE_LINKS_FILE to the staged set AND to the per-file idempotency basename set (so a pass changing only this file is still committed), with a test pinning both.

2. BLOCKING (under-invalidation, cycle shape): check_would_create_cycle walks the TRANSITIVE dependency graph, so a cycle can be broken by unlinking an INTERMEDIATE ticket while both endpoints stay byte-identical. My endpoint-only digest would not have noticed, suppressing a now-possible link indefinitely. Fixed: cycle records key on the global structural projection. Over-invalidating costs one extra attempt; under-invalidating suppresses a legitimate link forever — the asymmetry decides it. The narrow shapes stay endpoint-local so they do not churn.

3. BLOCKING (under-invalidation, hierarchy redirect): add_dependency calls resolve_hierarchy_link FIRST, which can REDIRECT an endpoint to a type-tier ancestor; the validators then run against that promoted ticket. So the deciding status can belong to an ancestor, not the id passed in. Fixed: the endpoint fingerprint now covers every ticket on the parent chain (status + deps each), which catches the redirect target wherever the promotion lands without re-deriving the promotion rule and drifting from it.

Also took the useful advisories: re-qualified records are pruned rather than left to accumulate, and a corrupt store degrades to empty and still attempts the write (both tested).

Plan review now PASSES and the attestation is certified (currency basis: file_impact). Each new behavioural test was RED-verified by temporarily reverting its specific mechanism. 19 tests in the new file; 2402 reconciler tests green; make lint and make typecheck exit 0.

compiled_state.description:
## Impact, stated first

Every live Reconcile Bridge pass re-attempts inbound (Jira -> rebar) link writes that **cannot ever succeed**: the source is closed, the relationship is redundant with the hierarchy, or the link would create a cycle. Each fails, logs a WARNING, and is forgotten; the next pass derives the identical set and tries again. The bridge **never converges**, and its log carries a permanent error floor that must be filtered before a real fault is visible.

## Evidence (measured 2026-08-12, live workflow logs)

Four consecutive live runs (31568815075, 31569179421, 31569723185, 31570037358, ~30 min) each emit exactly **19** failed inbound link writes: 5 `is closed`, 13 `redundant — ancestor-descendant`, 1 `would create a cycle`. Normalising and diffing two passes yields a **byte-identical** failing set. Passes re-dispatch every ~5-6 min: 200+ doomed writes/hour, indefinitely.

**Correction to the filing:** these are *local* `rebar link` subprocess writes, not Jira round-trips — real waste, but CPU/log cost rather than Jira API cost.

## Confirmed mechanism

- **Emitter:** `inbound_differ._diff_links_inbound` dedups an ADD only against the ticket's *current* local deps. A failed link never lands a LINK event, so the identical record is re-emitted every pass.
- **Applier:** `apply_inbound_records._inbound_update_apply_links`, `add` branch — `try: rebar.link(...) except Exception: logger.warning(...)`. That warn-and-continue is the whole handling.
- **Why permanent:** all three are raised by `graph/_links.py::add_dependency` from reduced local state — deterministic verdicts, not I/O faults; they re-raise identically until the *local structure* changes.
- **No durable memory anywhere:** the binding store holds only jira_key/state/baseline/peer-parent; `managed_refs` records only refs successfully created. Nothing records an attempt or a failure.

## Approach

Give the applier a durable, self-healing memory of *permanently impossible* inbound link ADDs, and consult it before spending the write.

1. **New module** `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/impossible_links.py`:
   - `classify(exc) -> reason | None` — classifies the three permanent shapes (`closed_source`, `redundant_ancestry`, `cycle`). Anything else returns `None`, behaviour unchanged. The safety valve: only provably-structural shapes are recorded.
   - `deciding_digest(source, target, relation, tracker_dir, reason)` — a stable digest over the structural inputs the *relevant* validator reads. This is the invalidation key: when it stops matching, the record is pruned and the link is attempted once more.
     - `closed_source` / `redundant_ancestry` are decided by the two endpoints, so those digests cover each endpoint's status, parent chain and dep set, undisturbed by edits elsewhere.
     - `cycle` is NOT endpoint-local: `add_dependency` walks the TRANSITIVE graph, so unlinking or reparenting an INTERMEDIATE ticket can break the cycle while both endpoints stay byte-identical. A cycle record therefore keys on the global structural projection (every ticket's status/parent/deps). Over-invalidating costs one extra attempt; under-invalidating would suppress a legitimate link indefinitely — the asymmetry decides it.
     - Non-structural edits (comments, titles) are excluded from every digest, so an unchanged structure converges to zero writes.
   - A JSON store at `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/impossible_links.json` (`version: 1`), keyed `source|target|relation` -> `{reason, digest, first_seen, last_seen, attempts}`. A **separate file** from `bindings.json`: no schema collision with the binding store or with the peer-confirmation record planned by epic despotic-floriated-leopard.
   - **The file must be COMMITTED to the tickets branch.** Each pass runs in a fresh CI checkout, so a record living only in the working tree is discarded between passes and the skip would never take effect in production — the bug would survive the fix with every unit test still green. `git_adapter.IMPOSSIBLE_LINKS_FILE` is added to the files `reconcile_helpers._commit_binding_store_snapshot` stages, and to its per-file idempotency basename set so a pass changing only this file is still committed.
   - **The endpoint fingerprint covers every ticket on the parent chain, not just the endpoint.** `add_dependency` calls `resolve_hierarchy_link` FIRST, which can REDIRECT an endpoint to a type-tier ancestor; the validators then run against that promoted ticket. So the deciding status/deps may belong to an ancestor. Fingerprinting the whole chain covers the redirect target wherever the promotion lands, without this module re-deriving the promotion rule and drifting from it.
2. **Applier change** (`_inbound_update_apply_links`, `add` branch only): before calling `rebar.link`, skip when a record matches the triple *and* its digest still matches. Otherwise attempt as today; on failure classify, and record only a permanent reason.
3. **Fail-open and hygiene:** a corrupt store, an uncomputable digest, or an unreducible ticket all degrade to "attempt the write", never "suppress it". Written by temp-file + atomic `os.replace`, only when something changed, so a converged pass touches the file zero times. A record whose digest stops matching is deleted, so dead entries cannot accumulate.
4. **Operator visibility:** a newly-recorded impossible link still WARNs exactly once, so a genuinely new one is loud. Subsequent skips log at DEBUG, plus one INFO summary per pass naming the count and store path. Deleting the JSON file re-qualifies everything — the manual clear.

**Out of scope:** the REMOVE branch, `_inbound_unlink_one`, and the differ's G3/G4/G5 suppression — that surface belongs to epic despotic-floriated-leopard. This change touches only the ADD branch and a distinct state file, so the two are complementary.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `classify` returns the correct reason for each of the three real error texts above, and `None` for a transient/unknown exception (unit test per shape).
- [ ] With a matching record and unchanged digest, `_inbound_update_apply_links` does **not** call `rebar.link` for that triple and does not count it in `links_applied`.
- [ ] When the deciding inputs change (the closed source is reopened), the digest stops matching and the link **is** re-attempted once.
- [ ] A failure that is not one of the three permanent shapes is **not** recorded and is retried next pass exactly as today.
- [ ] A first-time impossible link logs at WARNING; a subsequent skip does not.
- [ ] Steady-state evidence, not log suppression: over an unchanged store, pass 1 attempts the write and pass 2 performs **zero** `rebar.link` invocations (test counts facade calls, not log lines).
- [ ] The record survives a process restart — read back from the JSON by a fresh store instance.
- [ ] A structural change to an ANCESTOR of an endpoint (the ticket `resolve_hierarchy_link` promotes to) invalidates the record, even though the endpoint itself is unchanged (unit test).
- [ ] `impossible_links.json` is staged by `_commit_binding_store_snapshot` and present in its per-file idempotency set, so the record survives to the next pass (unit test).
- [ ] A `cycle` record is invalidated by a structural change to an INTERMEDIATE ticket (unlinking a third ticket that breaks the chain), even though both endpoints are unchanged — the under-invalidation trap (unit test comparing digests directly).
- [ ] A record whose digest stops matching is pruned from the store rather than left behind (unit test reading the JSON back).
- [ ] A corrupt/unparseable store degrades to empty and the link is still attempted (unit test).
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the existing inbound-link test files (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_inbound_links.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_removal_2b16.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_link_lands_locally_5200.py`) all pass unchanged.

file_impact.reason: New module: deterministic classification of permanently-impossible inbound link ADDs, the deciding-inputs digest, and the durable JSON skip store.
Consult the skip store before rebar.link in the ADD branch of _inbound_update_apply_links; classify and record permanent failures instead of warn-and-forget.
New behavioural tests: classification per error shape, skip-on-match, digest invalidation, transient-not-recorded, log levels, two-pass zero-write evidence, restart persistence.
